items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I don't want you to come in here and try to sound like Freddie Hubbard or anybody else, sound like you, you know.

ctx.x: You know, everybody would try -- maybe that's the trouble, everybody was trying too hard.

Well, you know, the young players should memorize everything the can. Now, not everybody can memorize, it's not easy. But there's a very lucky thing, there's an awful lot of solos transcribed now. And I know with my pupils, I give them a solo every week or every two weeks, of some famous solo, and I make them learn it like an etude. I say, don't come in here and bluff your way through it, learn that like you're practicing Arvins or ____, I don't give a damn. You learn that like an etude and I don't want you to…
And then I make them learn their chords on that solo, be able to play all the chords from that solo and all the scales associated with those chords. And then we pick another
